## Overview

Bound structured-output grammar compilation to `max(1, min(cpu_count // 2, 8))` by default, with `VLLM_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_MAX_COMPILE_WORKERS` as a positive-value override (0 = auto). Fixes #49460.

## Claims

- The default outer compile pool becomes 8 workers on a 172-core host, instead of 86, matching the existing fill-bitmask pool.
- Preserve current tokenizer initialization, grammar compilation, and fill-bitmask behavior; only compile-pool sizing changes.
- Allow operators to tune compile concurrency explicitly.

## Validation

Latest review fix: `f2477064684c` isolates the LLM worker-limit test's environment cache on entry and after environment restoration, including exceptional teardown. With a pre-enabled cache, the old setup read `(3, True)` rather than the requested `(1, False)`; the actual fixture now reads the overrides and restores the baseline after both success and failure. No production code changed in this follow-up. The CI bot merged 29 upstream commits as `05f7b93e0e2b` and started [Buildkite #98187](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98187). The 76 focused tests, fixture lifecycle smoke checks and test collection also pass on that merged head. The [full CodeRabbit review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49461#issuecomment-6417228252) completed on `05f7b93e0e2b` with no actionable comments. The new worker-limit regression now passes on both NVIDIA H200 MIG and AMD MI355 on this exact head; the overall build is not green (details below).

Local macOS/Python 3.12 validation:

```bash
VLLM_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_MAX_COMPILE_WORKERS=3 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest tests/v1/structured_output/test_compile_executor_sizing.py tests/v1/structured_output/test_regex_compilation_timeout.py tests/test_envs.py -q
# 76 passed, 1 package-version warning
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest --collect-only -q tests/entrypoints/llm/test_struct_output_generate.py -k compile_worker_limit
# 1 selected test collected
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files tests/entrypoints/llm/test_struct_output_generate.py
# All applicable hooks passed, including mypy and Buildkite test tethering
```

The helper run uses `--noconftest` because the repository-wide GPU teardown segfaults in torch.accelerator.empty_host_cache on this macOS host. On the preceding merged head `c28d0cdd706e`, 5 real structured-output-manager tests also passed with normal repository fixtures.

**GPU serving evidence on current head `05f7b93e0e2b`:** `test_structured_output_compile_worker_limit` executed and **PASSED** in both the [NVIDIA H200 MIG LLM shard](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98187#01a185c7-6951-4a8a-8fbb-ffcb838c6b05) and [AMD MI355 LLM shard](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98187#01a185c7-6968-461e-a3b9-169288795e16). It loads Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, checks the real manager's one-worker executor, and verifies constrained yes/no generation. All five NVIDIA/AMD LLM integration shards finished successfully.

**Remaining CI status:** [Buildkite #98187](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98187) has one completed failed lane: [H200 MIG LM Eval KV-Offload](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98187#01a185c7-69b3-49f0-98bd-219f49054ec7). `test_gsm8k_offloading_correctness[simple-nemotron-h-8b]` scored **0.3900 against a 0.4000 floor** on run 1/2 (1 failed, 3 passed, 5 deselected). The eval and KV-transfer files are unchanged from this merge's main parent, and the GSM8K request does not enable structured output. This is source-comparison evidence, not a reproduced main-branch GPU result or a confirmed root cause. #59818 documents variance in the same case on MI300; it does not establish the cause of this H200 failure. No tolerance or skip changes have been made. The remaining H200 PyTorch Fullgraph job passed at 05:21 UTC on October 29; no test jobs are still running. The blocked job-upload gate is not a test failure. The KV-Offload accuracy failure above is the only completed failed lane; [maintainer triage has been requested](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49461#issuecomment-6488529169).

Before/after decode latency under a container CPU quota has not been measured. The production observations in #49460 motivate the change; they are not benchmark results for this patch.

## Details

The reported production incident used a 6-CPU-limit pod on a 172-core host: the host-sized pool allowed CPU-heavy grammar compiles to compete with decode, with sustained CFS throttling and inter-token latency rising from 7–9 ms to 68–93 ms (RCA in #49460).

This is a bounded default, **not cgroup quota detection**. Eight workers can still exceed a smaller quota, and backend-internal compilation threads remain unchanged. Reducing concurrency may increase schema-burst compilation latency, especially on unconstrained hosts; operators can tune `VLLM_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_MAX_COMPILE_WORKERS`.

This updates the existing worker-cap PR rather than opening a duplicate. The open timeout proposals #54090 and #55597 bound individual compile duration, which is complementary to bounding concurrent compiles.

nodes.body: @mgoin @russellb — small self-contained fix for a production incident: the structured-output grammar-compile `ThreadPoolExecutor` is sized by host CPU count (cgroup-unaware), so on a Kubernetes pod with a low CPU limit on a 172-core host it spawns ~86 workers → sustained CFS throttling and decode stalls until requests hit the deadline (full metrics and RCA in #49460). It caps the pool to `max(1, min(cpu_count // 2, 8))` — mirroring the fill-bitmask pool created right above it — and adds `VLLM_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_MAX_COMPILE_WORKERS` as an operator override, with unit tests. DCO is signed. Could you review and add the `ready` label when you have a moment? Happy to adjust anything.

Recap: the grammar-compile `ThreadPoolExecutor` is sized from `multiprocessing.cpu_count()`, which is not cgroup-aware. Under a container CPU quota on a many-core host, the pool is created with far more workers than the quota allows, so a burst of structured-output requests fans CPU-bound compiles out past the quota, sustains CFS throttling, and stalls the engine loop until requests hit their deadline — with the GPU nearly idle the whole time. The fix caps the pool the same way the fill-bitmask pool right above it is capped, and adds an operator override. Details in #49460.

Small and self-contained — would appreciate a look whenever you have bandwidth.

## Overview

Bound structured-output grammar compilation to `max(1, min(cpu_count // 2, 8))` by default, with `VLLM_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_MAX_COMPILE_WORKERS` as a positive-value override (0 = auto). Fixes #49460.

## Claims

- The default outer compile pool becomes 8 workers on a 172-core host, instead of 86, matching the existing fill-bitmask pool.
- Preserve current tokenizer initialization, grammar compilation, and fill-bitmask behavior; only compile-pool sizing changes.
- Allow operators to tune compile concurrency explicitly.

## Validation

Latest review fix: `f2477064684c` isolates the LLM worker-limit test's environment cache on entry and after environment restoration, including exceptional teardown. With a pre-enabled cache, the old setup read `(3, True)` rather than the requested `(1, False)`; the actual fixture now reads the overrides and restores the baseline after both success and failure. No production code changed in this follow-up. The CI bot merged 29 upstream commits as `05f7b93e0e2b` and started [Buildkite #98187](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98187). The 76 focused tests, fixture lifecycle smoke checks and test collection also pass on that merged head. The [full CodeRabbit review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49461#issuecomment-6417228252) completed on `05f7b93e0e2b` with no actionable comments. The new worker-limit regression now passes on both NVIDIA H200 MIG and AMD MI355 on this exact head; the overall build is not green (details below).
